newsitem.title: UK: IPE oil slump deepens as bull run fades.
newsitem.headline: IPE oil slump deepens as bull run fades.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures went into a steep slide on Thursday, finalling breaking the back of a four-month-long bull run.
Dealers said the slide was led by a technical turnaround on U.S. markets where crude and gasoline led the way lower.
But they said news that two rival Kurdish factions had agreed to extend a U.S. brokered ceasefire in northern Iraq had also undermined the oil market.
December Brent by 1925 GMT was down 87 cents at $22.74 a barrel, $2.30 below its peak in mid-October.
"This is meltdown," said broker Tim Holmes at MeesPierson Derivatives. "It's more than your average correction."
Dealers said financial hedge funds helped drive prices lower as local speculators sparked computerised stop-loss sell orders.
"We went through some important technical stops and that triggered the hedge funds," said a broker. The break below $24 for December NYMEX crude was particularly significant, he said.
In Ankara U.S. envoy Robert Pelletreau said rival Kurdish groups had agreed to extend a ceasefire in northern Iraq with a view to making it permanent.
The UN-Iraqi oil-for-food exchange was put on hold at the end of August when clashes made it unsafe for UN monitors in the region.
"I suppose this puts oil-for-food back on the map but that's not the real reason this market came off," said a dealer in London.
